chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ja'far ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Abd Allah, from his father, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: A thief steals in one year, then is brought before the governor so that he may carry out the cutting on him, but he is pardoned. Then he is seized in the following year after having committed a second theft, and is brought before the ruler. For which of the two thefts is the cutting carried out? He said: “He is to be cut for the latter one, and he is to be made to strive regarding the property that he stole the first time until he returns it to its owner.”

key_terms.السَّارِقُ: the thief who committed the theft
key_terms.السَّرِقَتَيْنِ: the two acts of theft under discussion
key_terms.السُّلْطَانِ: the ruler or authority administering legal punishment
key_terms.الْوَالِي: the governing authority before whom the accused is brought
key_terms.صَاحِبِهِ: the rightful owner of the stolen property
key_terms.يُسْتَسْعَى: he is made to exert himself to repay or restore what is owed
key_terms.يُقْطَعُ: the hadd punishment of amputation is carried out

ai.seo_question: If a thief was pardoned after one theft and then steals again later, for which theft is the hadd punishment applied?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a thief who committed one theft, was not punished at that time, and later committed another theft. Imam Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام states that the hadd is applied for the later theft, while the stolen property from the earlier theft remains a financial liability that must be returned to its owner.
